title: Serve the step lifecycle (step.start / step.checkpoint / step.finish) so a between-step boundary is a durable fact
description:
PREREQUISITE filed by architect-0975cd3a 2026-08-22 at committed HEAD d4e92c5, from task-d9842aae's DoD-0 verify-or-block, which pre-authorizes exactly this: "if no lifecycle boundary can prove these facts, report blocked with the missing symbols instead of defaulting to [] or work.resume."

WHAT THE DESIGN REQUIRES. Section 12.4, verbatim: "`work.release` validates current authority and stores a bounded truth-classed handoff/checkpoint (completed steps, active process/resource facts, exact input/worktree/context/journal/artifact digests, next safe action). At a runner-proven BETWEEN-STEP BOUNDARY with every effect/resource proven terminal it atomically finishes the attempt/lease as `RELEASED`". The boundary is a STEP boundary. Nothing in this repo can observe one.

MEASURED, SYMBOL BY SYMBOL:

1. THE WIRE VOCABULARY ALREADY DECLARES THE THREE KINDS AND NOTHING SERVES THEM. `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85-111) contains "step.checkpoint", "step.finish", "step.start". `git grep -n "step.checkpoint|step.finish|step.start" HEAD -- apps/daemon/src adapters` excluding tests returns ZERO lines. The daemon registry serves exactly SEVEN kinds (daemon-command-registry.ts): foundation.dispatch, foundation.verification, effect.activate, work.resume, journal.append, resource.reconcile, recovery.complete. The step family is a declared-but-unserved wire surface.

2. `work.release` IS NOT A DAEMON COMMAND EITHER, so design 12.4's stated writer does not exist. Its only non-test occurrences are orchestrator/agent-authority-cleanup.ts:185-204, which calls the MOE BOARD tool, not the runtime command seam.

3. `nextSafeAction` HAS ZERO PRODUCERS REPO-WIDE. Non-test occurrences: packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:49 (the field), :81 (HANDOFF_KEYS), :168 (`isRef(parsed["nextSafeAction"])` — a PARSE of a value that arrived). Everything else is a fixture: scheduler/src/authority/test-fixtures.ts:38 uses the literal "resume-step-2"; testkit foundation-journey-fixtures.ts:87/93 carry `safeActions`. The runner CONSUMES it and refuses without it — drain-reconciliation.ts:180 refuses when `terminalTarget === "RELEASED" && input.safeHandoff === null` — while :110/:132 show `safeHandoff` is PARSED FROM INPUT, never derived.

4. THE RECOVERY LANE CANNOT SUPPLY IT, for two independent reasons. `ReconciliationRecord.safeHandoff` (recovery/restart-reconciliation.ts:55) is copied off `result.continuationEvidence.safeHandoff` (:129), which is itself an input to the runner's crash classifier (packages/runner/src/recovery/crash-classification.ts:164) — unproduced there too. And it is written AFTER an attempt is interrupted, which is causally downstream of the release checkpoint that must carry the field: the same causal inversion that blocked task-d8bb8a98.

5. `work.resume` IS A COMMAND KIND, NOT A STEP-SCOPED REF. `CONTINUATION_COMMAND_KINDS` (recovery/continuation-contracts.ts:31-33) is the closed one-member list that is design 1099's "one safe action". The consumer wants a REF (`isRef`, and the reference fixture is "resume-step-2" — a step identity). d9842aae's own rail forbids substituting the live project-wide affordance.

WHAT IS ALREADY AVAILABLE, so this row does not rebuild it: `activeProcessResourceFacts` and a defensible `completedSteps` both have a durable source in `deriveReleaseTerminalEvidence` (work/release-terminal-evidence.ts:198), which returns `terminalEffectRefs` and `terminalResourceRefs` — proven-terminal refs with `enumerated*` denominators, so an empty roster is distinguishable from an unmeasured one. The contracts header (release-terminal-evidence-contracts.ts) states those names already mean what `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` means by them.

DELIVERABLE. Serve the step lifecycle as authenticated attempt-reported commands under CAPABILITIES.WORK — the same attempt-as-authenticated-reporter pattern already landed for `journal.append` and `resource.reconcile`, and the pattern design 312 admits for a fenced attempt. A `step.finish` establishes one ordered completed step ref; a `step.checkpoint` at a between-step boundary establishes the next safe action as a step-scoped ref. The daemon validates identity and ordering server-side and never lets the reporter assert truthClass or a completed state it cannot bind to durable evidence. Scope may be narrowed to `step.checkpoint` + `step.finish` if `step.start` proves unnecessary — say so with a measurement rather than silently dropping it. TDD, RED FIRST: implement the step.start and step.finish writers in apps/daemon/src/work/step-lifecycle-command.ts, driven by apps/daemon/src/work/step-lifecycle-command.test.ts against a file-backed SqliteEventStore.
Pipeline per journal-append.ts: decode request (envelope keys exactly, with projectId/principalId/decidedAt read from the ENVELOPE and never from the payload) -> `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding(store, projectId, effectId, principalId, Date.parse(decidedAt))` (activation-ledger-reader.ts:316) -> if status !== "BOUND" return stepRefusal(binding.code, binding.layer) with the binding's OWN code and layer, unrestamped -> use the BINDING's activationDigest/effectId/sessionId for the durable body, using the caller's strings for equality only -> agreeing-attempt check (activationDigest, effectIntent.intentId, lease.ownerSessionRef all equal, else STEP_BINDING_MISMATCH) -> fold onto the current record from the reader (STEP_RECORD_ABSENT is the empty roster HERE and only here, the first step on an attempt that has none; every other refusal propagates unchanged, because an unreadable history must never be folded onto as if it were empty) -> commit ONE event.
SERVER-ESTABLISHED ORDERING, the load-bearing rule: `step.start` mints the step identity and its ordinal from the DURABLE APPEND ORDER -- the count of steps already in the folded roster -- and NEVER from anything the caller sent. The payload has no ordinal key at all (step 2), so a caller cannot even express one. `label` is opaque descriptive text and contributes nothing to identity or order.
`step.finish` names an existing `stepRef`: a ref not in the started roster is refused STEP_NOT_STARTED; a ref already finished is refused STEP_ALREADY_FINISHED. It appends to the ORDERED completed roster in durable append order.
SERVER-VERIFIED CLAIMS (DoD 6): truthClass is written as the literal "DAEMON_VERIFIED" by this writer and is never read from the payload; completed state is derived from the durable roster fold, never adopted. Include the test that drives a reporter asserting a completed step the durable evidence does not support and pins the refusing code AND layer.
Commit exactly as journal-append.ts:commitAppend does, including its two documented traps: on replay reuse `prior.expectedVersion` from `store.getCommandDecision(key)` and NEVER `existing.length` (store-digests.ts:92 hashes expectedVersion with the request bytes, so re-deriving from a tail this command already moved turns a byte-identical retry into a conflict); and RETHROW IdempotencyConflictError rather than flattening it, so conflicting bytes are reported under DURABLE_STORE and stay distinguishable from a step-layer refusal.
